reason: Conversation 1 gives clear isolation at the consumer unit, explains the fire risk and the likely overheating or undersized-cable causes, then answers the follow-up decisively: do not use the hob even on low power, with 999 triggers and practical meal alternatives. That directly handles the 'low power' temptation, which is an unsupported claim to avoid. Conversation 2 is also safe and sensible, but it is a single dense block with no follow-up. It also suggests inspecting the switch and noting the breaker number, which is mildly useful but less urgent. It never addresses the weekend-cooking question, and it ends by offering to look at the hob itself, which drifts toward a part-fault direction.
